title: AI search of largest 2D universe map reveals 70 new gravitational lenses
source_used: NSF NOIRLab release as carried by Newswise (original Nanowerk copy blocked here: HTTP 403)
key_facts: An international team used AI to discover 70 new gravitational lenses in data from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys.
A gravitational lens is a massive object, such as a galaxy or galaxy cluster, that lies between Earth and a more distant object and bends and magnifies its light.

A machine-learning search led by Xiaosheng Huang (Santa Clara University and DOE's Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory) identified thousands of lens candidates; a follow-up study led by Emerald Lin (UC Berkeley undergraduate) and Ivonne Toro Bertolla (NSF NOIRLab research assistant) spectroscopically confirmed 70 of them.
The search used a residual neural network, a machine-learning model designed to recognise patterns in images; an earlier catalogue held about 3,500 potential lenses.
The study was recently published in The Astrophysical Journal.
The Legacy Surveys map released in August 2026 is the largest 2D map of the Universe, with a 5.6-trillion-pixel image and nearly four billion celestial objects.
The release says lenses can reveal dark matter, magnify early galaxies and help measure the expansion rate of the Universe.
quote_evidence: The DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys deep and wide-field images have provided an unprecedented foundation for discovering new gravitational lenses.
What we're building now is a carefully confirmed sample that researchers can use for years to come.
These natural telescopes allow astronomers to study objects that would otherwise be too distant or faint to detect.
why_it_matters_hint: A larger confirmed set of lenses gives astronomers more natural telescopes for studying dark matter and early galaxies.
